title: Skew and hot keys
summary: Detect skew when a small number of keys create disproportionately large partitions or slow tasks.

blocks.text: Detect skew when a small number of keys create disproportionately large partitions or slow tasks.

items: Compare task durations and shuffle read sizes across a stage.
Null/unknown keys can become accidental hot keys.
AQE skew handling can split skewed partitions in supported workloads.
Manual salting is a targeted technique with correctness and complexity costs.

blocks.question: What is the first evidence of skew you should look for?
blocks.answer: A stage where a small number of tasks process much more data or run much longer than their peers, confirmed by key-frequency and partition-size inspection.
